content.comment_body: Dear [product_name] user, today the free [product_name] Access Tool has been released on the [company_name] website. Enjoy working with [product_name]!
Could you provide a clearer link? The current one seems to point to logo-related content.
Here is a direct link to the Access Tool: [url]
Hello [user_name], does this show variables for timers such as I/O? If so, could you explain how to view them? Thanks.
Check the help documentation attached. Timers and counters cannot be copied directly into Excel with the Access Tool. You need to use VM mapping for this purpose.

analysis.insight_summary: Community members engaged with the announcement of the [product_name] Access Tool, asking for a more precise download link and clarification on its features, particularly regarding timer and counter data export to Excel. The responses reveal that the tool does not support direct export of such variables and reference documentation for further instructions, showing a gap between user expectations and provided functionality.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a straightforward method to access all device variables, including timers and counters, and to export these directly to Excel, without needing extra configuration like VM mapping.
